full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Akram Hossain Chowdhury, J :-This Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the inclusion of the petitioner's building situated on Plot No.20/2, Block-C, Mohammadpur, Dhaka, as an abandoned property published in the "Kha" list of Extra Ordinary Bangladesh Gazette on 23.9.1986 and the judgment and order dated 15.01.2001 passed by the 1st Court of Settlement. Shegunbagicha, Dhaka, in Settlement Case No.186 of 1995 (Kha-44, Block-C, Mohammadpur, Dhaka), relating to House No.20/2, Block-C, Mohammadpur. Dhaka (Annexure-I-1) should not be declared to have been passed without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this akin may seem fit and proper. 

 3. Further contention of the writ petition is that Syed Moamber Reza son of Nasim Zohora also acquired an allotment of holding No.20/1, which is adjacent to holding No.20/2 of Block-C, Mohammadpur Housing Estate, Mohammadpur, Dhaka, from the Government. Thereafter, both Syed Moamber Reza, and his mother Nasim Zohora jointly by a registered sale, deed dated .10.2.1971 sold out their respective holding No.20/1 and 20/2 of Block-C. Mohammadpur Housing Estate, Dhaka, to one Mrs. Rafia Khatun. The present petitioner by way of a registered sale deed dated 10.11.1973 purchased the holding No.20/2 from the- said Mrs. Rafia Khatun and possessing the same paying rent and taxes to the concern authorities. Petitioner then filed an application to the Assistant Commissioner, Housing and Settlement Office, Ministry of Works, Segunbagicha, Dhaka, for mutating his name in place of the name of his vendor i.e. Rafia Khatun. The settlement office, accordingly, enquired into the matter and submitted a report thereon. In spite of a favourable report the respondent No.2 illegally included the case house in the "Kha" list of abandoned property. Then, the petitioner filed a petition  before the respondent No.1 i.e. the Court of Settlement under Section 7 of the Abandoned Buildings (Supplementary Provisions), Ordinance LIV of 1985 for exclusion of the building from the abandoned list, which was registered as settlement Case No.186 of 1995. 

 13. With respect to the submissions as advanced by the learned advocate for the petitioner that no statutory notice was served upon the petitioner before enlisting the property in the "Kha" list of the abandoned property. It is pertinent to mention here that our apex Court in the case of Rowshan Ara Begum -Vs- Secretary, Ministry of Works and Urban Development, Government of Bangladesh and others, reported in 59 DLR (AD)-165 decided the matter holding that- 

 It is also decided in the case of Government of Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Works -Vs- Md. Jalil and others, reported in 48 DLR (AD)-10, that the onus squarely lies upon the claimant to prove his claim. In the said decision the apex Court held that- 

 In view of the facts and circumstances and discussions made herein above we are of the that the petitioner has failed to prove his claim that the property in question is not an abandoned property. As such we do not find any reason to interfere with the impugned judgment and order dated 15.01.2001 passed by the First Court of Settlement, Dhaka, in Settlement Case No.186 of 1995. 

 14. In the result, the rule is discharged without however any order as to costs. The judgment and order dated 15.1.2001 passed by the 1st  Court of Settlement, Sheunbagicha, Dhaka in Settlement Case No.186 of 1995 (Ka-44, Block-C, Mohammadpur, Dhaka) in respect of House No.20/2, Block-C, Mohammadpur, Dhaka is hereby declared to have been passed legally lawfully and having its jurisdiction.
